title: Subramania Bharati: Fearless We Stand!
culture_region: India / Greece / USA / South Africa / World
summary: 'Even if the skies collapse upon our heads, fearless, fearless, fearless we stand!' sang Bharati, transforming Tamil poetry into a roaring weapon of liberation.
full_text:
In 1908, in the city of Madras, the British colonial authorities trembled at the words of a twenty-five-year-old poet with a twisted mustache and turban: Mahakavi C. Subramania Bharati.

Editing the revolutionary weekly *India*, printed on eye-catching red paper, Bharati poured fiery verses into the hearts of Tamil youth:
"When will this thirst for freedom be slaked?
When will our love of servitude be shattered?"

Armed British police stormed his press, brandishing an arrest warrant for sedition, threatening him with exile to the Andaman Cellular Jail.

Bharati stood tall, his dark eyes ablaze with divine fire. Looking straight into the eyes of the armed officers, he began to sing with thunderous resonance:

**"Achamillai, Achamillai, Acham Enbathillaiye!
Ichagathu lor elam ethirthu nindra pothinum,
Achamillai, Achamillai, Acham Enbathillaiye!
Uchi meethu vaan idinthu veezhukinra pothinum,
Achamillai, Achamillai, Acham Enbathillaiye!**

(Fear we have none, fear we have none, fear we know not!
Even if the entire cosmos rises in enmity against us,
Fear we have none!
Even if the vault of heaven shatters and falls upon our heads,
Fear we have none!)"

The colonial police stood spellbound by the overwhelming power of his spirit.

To preserve his freedom to write, Bharati slipped across the border to French-controlled Pondicherry, where in extreme poverty he authored his immortal masterpieces: *Kannan Pattu*, *Panchali Sabatham*, and *Kuyil Pattu*.

Bharati demonstrated that tyrants may possess bayonets, but a poet's song can awaken a nation to unyielding fearlessness.
moral: Fearlessness is the foundation of freedom; when the human spirit casts out fear, oppression loses all power.
